title: Evaluating the Accuracy of Owner‐Reported Sex Determination of Pet African Grey Parrots (Psittacus erithacus) From Urban Households Through DNA Analysis and Implications for Conservation
content:
ABSTRACT

Sex determination in parrots based on external morphology remains challenging, particularly in African grey parrots (Psittacus erithacus), which lack pronounced sexual dimorphism. In this study, we evaluated the accuracy of morphological sex assignment in pet African grey parrots by comparing owner-reported phenotypic sex with molecular genotyping of the sex-linked chromohelicase-DNA-binding gene. Among 715 individuals sampled during a national registration exercise, 44.6% were found to be misdiagnosed based on morphology, while 9% could not be assigned a sex by owners using morphology. Females were more frequently misclassified as males, likely due to the absence of egg-laying behaviour as a visual cue. Morphometric analysis revealed no significant differences between males and females in the traits measured. These findings highlight widespread inaccuracies in phenotypic sex assignment across captive populations. We discuss these findings and possible implications for breeding management, community-based conservation efforts and potential species reintroduction programmes.
